output_files.coverage_honesty: This is 1 edition out of 635 in F&G, and 0 editions of C&E. It is NOT the full family. Sampled edition is a 2011 EURO1 FRR (RHD) — an early, smaller catalogue than a late EURO6 edition, so the per-edition yield elsewhere will differ.

f_series_answer.epc_side: One edition alone yields 4,023 distinct part numbers. The whole F&G family is 635 such editions, so the true part-number count is in the hundreds of thousands, not the low hundreds. The family is unambiguously much bigger than a euro-ranked decode can see.
f_series_answer.overlap_with_the_95: Of the 4,023 EPC part numbers from this one edition, only 6 appear in the cross-reference's F-only list. 4,017 have no PMS vehicle record at all.
f_series_answer.why_that_matters: That is the same coverage defect the brief describes, measured: the cross-reference only knows the handful of F-series parts that were salient enough to be catalogued by hand from billing, while the EPC lists thousands per edition. The sliver is a coverage artefact.
f_series_answer.crossref_anchored_counts: Re-derived with an ANCHORED match on genuine_bvp_crossref.csv: F-only 44, N-only 15, shared 0, so F total 44. The unanchored script prints 95 because its marker list contains a bare 'F*' that substring-matches 'TF*' (D-Max).

f_series_vs_95.what_was_withdrawn: The '95 of 95' part numbers and the EUR 1,955,749 attributed to them are withdrawn. This probe recorded them at the time as the brief's figures; they do not reproduce and must not be quoted.
f_series_vs_95.how: reran 01_data/91_build/pn_ammo_probe_20260918/_f_vs_n_breadth.py - it prints 'F-series only PNs : 81', 'N-series only PNs : 45', 'shared / both : 13' -> 81+13 = 94 distinct F PNs, reported to Jerome earlier as '95 of 95' and 'EUR 1,955,749' across 11 service categories. Those counts came from an unanchored marker and that euro rested on pickup blower filters; both are withdrawn.
f_series_vs_95.important_defect_found_in_that_marker: The marker used by _f_vs_n_breadth.py is_is_f() is NOT anchored: any(k in s for k in ('FRR','FSR','FTR','FVR','FVM','FSS','FTS','FVZ','F*')). The token 'F*' substring-matches 'TF*' (the D-Max pickup). Measured on genuine_bvp_crossref.csv: vehicle_model merely CONTAINS 'F' -> 219 distinct PNs; vehicle_model begins 'TF' (D-Max) -> 62 of those. An anchored whole-token match returns 56 PNs from 82 rows. The corrected size is measured on the family table, not here: vehicle_family_bands.csv carries 164 heavy truck part numbers billing EUR 174,832 in 2025 on a 1,238-vehicle fleet.
f_series_vs_95.catalogue_side: TRUCKS F&G ALONE has 635 editions versus the ~94 F PNs the cross-reference knows. That is the family-is-much-bigger-than-the-decode-shows direction, but editions are NOT distinct part numbers, so this does NOT quantify the answer.

transport_finding.detail_1: The only channel available to this subagent is browser_cdp (MCP), whose result returns into the model context. A 968-edition crawl is millions of tokens if routed that way, so it cannot be run as-is.
transport_finding.detail_2: The script bridge the sibling agent used earlier - node 01_data/91_build/epc_batch2/cdp_eval.js <viewId> <expr> - now fails with 'no DevToolsActivePort found'. That file is written by the browser on startup; a recursive search of %USERPROFILE%\.cursor and %LOCALAPPDATA%\Cursor found none, so the browser appears to have been restarted with the debug port closed.
transport_finding.consequence: The controller 01_data/91_build/epc_catalogue/scrape_epc_catalogue.js is sound and was NOT rewritten, but its results have no disk route in this session. A session with browser_cdp AND a working CDP script bridge (or the collector on 127.0.0.1:8793 plus a page that can reach loopback) is required to finish.
